title: Discovery, pricing and your first paid no-code clients

say: Discovery, pricing, and your first paid no-code clients.
This is the video for module three of No-Code App Development.
Builders who skip discovery build the app the client described, which is often not the app the client needs.

items: Find the real process and its cost

say: In this video you will learn to find the real problem, price your work without underpricing yourself, and plan your first 90 days of paid work.

say: Discovery is the conversation and observation you do before quoting. Ask for the real steps, and for the last time it went wrong.

panel.heading: Six questions that find the real problem
items: Walk me through what happens, start to finish
Where does it go wrong? The last time?
How long does each step take, how often?
Who enters data, who reads it, what phones?
Can I see the notebook or sheet you use now?
In three months, how will you know it worked?

say: Measure time, and find out who uses the data and on what phones.

say: Ask to see the real notebook, and agree a success measure. Then watch the process happen once, even for 20 minutes. People describe their work as tidier than it is.

say: For example, Ruth is secretary of a thrift cooperative in Owerri with 48 members. She records each weekly payment from transfer screenshots, about 3 minutes per member.

panel.heading: What Ruth's process costs today
items: 48 members x 3 minutes = 144 minutes a week
2.4 hours x 4 weeks = 9.6 hours
Plus 5 hours reconciliation = 14.6 hours
Twice last quarter: a paid member told she owed

say: That is 2.4 hours a week, and with month-end reconciliation, 14.6 hours a month.

say: And twice last quarter, a member was wrongly told she had not paid. Ruth first asked for an app where members log in. But the real pain was her own time and the disputes, which a much smaller internal app solves.

panel.rule: Measure hours and errors now, so you can show the improvement later.

say: Write each need as a user story: as the secretary, I want to record a payment by choosing a member, so I stop rewriting names. Must stories make the app useful at all.

panel.heading: Sort user stories with MoSCoW
items: Must: record payments, flag unpaid by Friday
Should: monthly statement as a PDF
Could: a contributions chart
Won't this time: member log-in

say: Should and Could stories can follow. Won't means not this time. Put it all on a one-page specification, and get the client's approval in writing, even by WhatsApp, before you quote a final price.

say: Underpricing is the most common mistake, because clicking in the editor is quick. Estimate every phase: discovery 6 hours, setup 4, building 16, testing 6, and training 4. That is 36 hours.
At 10,000 naira an hour, that is 360,000 naira. Add 15 percent for unknowns.

say: Tie each payment to something the client can see. 40 percent when the specification is approved, 40 percent when the test version is shown, and 20 percent at go-live.

say: Keep three costs clearly separate. Your build fee.

cards.d: Paid to you once, in milestones, for discovery, building, testing and training.
The client pays the vendor directly, under an account the client owns.
A monthly retainer or hourly support, after a short free warranty such as 14 days.

say: The platform fee, which the client pays directly. For three officers on Starter, about US$15 a month. If you pay it for them, the app stops the day your card fails.

say: And support. For example, a retainer of 4 hours a month, which is 40,000 naira at 10,000 an hour. A defect is something that does not work as specified. A new idea is a change.

say: Scope creep is the slow growth of the job through small extra requests. Each sounds tiny. Together they eat your profit. First, thank the client and check the specification.

panel.heading: Handle extra requests calmly
items: Thank the client
Check it against the specification
If new, give an hour estimate
Ask: add it now, or next phase?
Record it in your change log

say: If it is new, estimate the hours and ask whether to add it now or later. Log the date, request, hours and approval, so the final invoice has no surprises.

panel.rule: New requests are estimated in hours and approved in writing.

say: Payment scams target freelancers too. Never start work on a transfer alert screenshot. Confirm the money in your own account before each milestone.

cards.d: Never start work on a screenshot. Confirm the money in your own account first.
Be wary of overpayments followed by requests to refund the difference.
Share the sheet only with officers. Never store bank logins, BVN or card numbers.

say: For example, Aisha in Kano chooses stock and sales apps for shops. She builds two demo apps with made-up sample data. Never show a real client's customers.

panel.heading: Aisha's plan for paid work
items: Weeks 1-4: build two demo apps
Weeks 5-8: contact 40 shops, 10 a week
Aim for 6 conversations and 3 proposals
Weeks 9-12: win and deliver first builds

say: Then she contacts 40 shops through her market association, aiming for 6 discovery conversations and 3 proposals.

say: To remember. Watch the work and measure what it costs. Keep version one small. Price every phase. Keep the three costs separate. And always confirm payment in your own account.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Watch the work and measure its cost
Keep version one to the Must stories
Estimate every phase and add contingency
Separate build fee, platform fee and support
Confirm payment in your own account
